answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The shale multiplier is published, charged in nectar, and vertex lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3387 identities would post 2008 proofs and burn roughly 81 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
